Intel cratered 28.6% after guiding Q4 revenue to a range of $15 billion to $16 billion, below what it just reported, briefly pulling QQQ into correction territory intraday.

Apple surpassed NVIDIA as the most valuable company at $5 trillion while Amazon CEO Andy Jassy pledged roughly $220 billion in 2026 capital spending.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and NVIDIA didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat NVDA. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

The Nasdaq-100 spent part of Friday, October 30, 2026, below the line that defines a correction, then climbed back above it before the close. It fell 3.46% to close at 28,384.85, after reaching an intraday low of 28,093.24.

Who is Danny / Shutterstock.com

That low sat 10.0% below the October 6 record close of 31,224.47. A correction means a 10% drop from a record, so the index crossed that line during the session. It closed 9.1% below the record, which means it never finished a day in correction.

Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) closed at $690.49, down 3.47%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.86% to 25,437.00, its lowest close since July 31.

The selling started in chips. Shares of Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) fell 28.6% after it guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15 billion to $16 billion, below the $16.5 billion it had just reported. Joe Tigay, a portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, said, "We're moving out of the hopes and dreams phase of the AI trade and into the 'show me' phase."

Why the Close Matters More Than the Intraday Low

The correction label is based on closing prices, and buyers came in before the close and raised the index back above the line. Volatility followed the same path. The VIX, which measures how much investors expect the S&P 500 to swing, hit 23.93 during the session but closed at 19.41, up 12.91%.

QQQE holds the same 100 NASDAQ stocks as QQQ but caps each position near 1%, slashing concentration risk for retirees.

QQQ holds about 8 times more NVIDIA per dollar than QQQE, and Apple shows a similar 6-to-1 gap between the two funds.

QQQE beat QQQ over the past year (15% vs. 13%) but badly trailed over 10 years (296% vs. 511%).

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Apple didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat AAPL. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Most people who buy Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) want broad exposure to the NASDAQ-100. That portfolio leans heavily on a few chipmakers and tech platforms. Retirees and near-retirees who like the growth of those 100 companies but don't want so much riding on a few of them can look at a smaller fund. It holds the same holdings on very different terms: the Direxion NASDAQ-100 Equal Weighted Index ETF (NASDAQ:QQQE).

Spencer Platt / Getty Images
NVIDIA Holds 7.6% of QQQ but Under 1% of QQQE

QQQ seeks to track the investment results, before fees and expenses, of the Nasdaq-100 Index, and it weights each company by market value. As of June 30, 2026, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) was its largest holding at 7.60% of net assets. QQQE owns the same company, but as of July 31, 2026, NVIDIA made up only 0.97% of the fund. Using those two filing dates, QQQ held about 7.8 times as much NVIDIA per dollar invested.

------

The same pattern holds. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) was 6.67% of QQQ as of June 30, compared with 1.01% of QQQE as of July 31. That's a ratio of roughly 6.6 to 1. The two filings are a month apart, so the weights have moved since then. The gap itself is built in, though. QQQE regularly rebalances every holding back to a roughly equal piece, while QQQ lets its biggest winners keep growing.

Six Giants Take Up a Third of QQQ

In QQQ's June 30 filing, its six largest holdings, led by NVIDIA and Apple, added up to about 32.4% of the fund. In QQQE's July 31 filing, those same six names came to roughly 5.9%. QQQE's equity weights ran from 0.4425047962% to 1.3017191224%, and most positions sat near 1%. The money that QQQ puts into its giants is spread across health care, industrials, utilities, consumer and software companies. In QQQ, those companies get much smaller slices.

Shares of Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) fell 28.73% in Friday's session and traded at $65.62 as of 9:44 AM ET. The catalyst is the chipmaker's third-quarter earnings report, released after Thursday's close. Same-day headlines tie the broader tech sell-off to Intel's results, with Reuters reporting that the report amplified AI spending worries across the NASDAQ. If you own a NASDAQ-100 or semiconductor index fund, part of this loss lands in your account too.

DaveAlan / iStock Unreleased via Getty Images

The fall started before Friday. Intel was already down 23.24% over the past week and 43.4% over the past month.

Weak Guidance Overshadowed an Earnings Beat

On the surface, the quarter looked solid. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $0.52, ahead of the $0.3953 consensus, and revenue of $16.51 billion came in slightly above estimates. Data Center and AI revenue rose 78% year over year to $7.32 billion.

------

The outlook told a different story. Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue to $15.0 billion to $16.0 billion and non-GAAP EPS to $0.25. It expects client revenue to fall greater than 20% sequentially as PC makers cut inventory. An extended shutdown at Intel's Israel factory is expected to reduce Q4 revenue by about $300 million and gross margin by 200 basis points. The CFO also said Intel did not expect positive free cash flow in 2027, adding, "We are not optimistic about next year in terms of memory." CEO Lip-Bu Tan said, "I'm disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter."

In QQQ, Intel was a top-10 position worth $14.9 billion, larger than the fund's stakes in Broadcom and Meta at the time. In the S&P 500 fund, Intel did not appear among the 10 largest holdings. The smallest of those 10 weighed 1.57%, so Intel's share of a plain S&P 500 index fund is modest.

What Friday's Drop Means for Fund Returns

Applying Friday's fall to the June 30 weights gives a rough estimate of Intel's drag. That works out to about 1.48 percentage points for SMH and about 0.87 percentage points for QQQ, from Intel alone. Treat these as estimates. Weights shift as prices move, and Intel's share price has swung from $103.79 at its July earnings filing to $93.09 at Thursday's filing. Headlines also show the NASDAQ falling broadly, so each fund's total move today reflects more than Intel.

Overlap Risk Hits Retirement Savers Hardest

Concentration becomes a problem when you pile funds that hold the same stocks. NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) was SMH's largest position at 17.55%. Together, NVIDIA and Intel made up about 22.7% of SMH. In QQQ, NVIDIA held 7.60%, and the two chipmakers combined for about 10.64%. NVIDIA was also the S&P 500 fund's top holding at 7.58%.

A 401(k) or IRA holding an S&P 500 core fund, QQQ for growth, and SMH as a sector tilt owns the same chip names three times. On a quiet day, that overlap goes unnoticed. On a day like Friday, it adds up. Investors close to retirement have less time to recover from sector shocks, so it is worth adding up your total semiconductor exposure across every fund you own.

Key Signals to Track From Here

Intel expected the Israel factory to restart by the end of the week of the call, though management said the impact on the first quarter could be similar to Q4. The company said it has secured about 40% more substrate capacity, with much of it arriving in the second half of 2027. Tan also said Intel expects "a couple of customers ready to announce" for advanced packaging over the next two quarters. Fund holdings are reported with a lag, so check each sponsor's latest list for current weightings, and keep an eye on the stock as index funds rebalance.

Amazon's Earnings Miss Exposes a Deepening Cash Squeeze

Q4 2026 net sales guidance from Amazon of $240 billion to $247 billion straddled the $244.5 billion Wall Street analysts expected, but its center fell short. Operating income guidance from Amazon of $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion trailed the $32.99 billion Wall Street analysts expected at the center.

The Invesco QQQ Trust, which tracks the Nasdaq-100, is poised to end the month lower.

Among Asian markets, the iShares MSCI South Korea ETF is down the most this month, declining more than 11% as of Oct. 29.

Korean-listed shares of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix were down about 17% and 20%, respectively, in October.

Global stock markets are headed for a mixed close in October, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 poised to end higher, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq and Asian markets lag amid a volatile month for technology stocks.

Asian markets, including China, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, are trending lower as tech-related weakness, central bank policy updates, and inflation concerns weigh on stocks.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

US Markets Vs Asia Markets

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) are headed higher this month, holding strong amid a massive U.S. tech selloff.

DIA leads, up nearly 3% so far, while SPY is set to close about 1% higher.

Meanwhile, the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq-100, is poised to end the month lower as investors grow wary of the sustainability of returns on massive AI infrastructure investments.

Among Asian markets, the iShares MSCI South Korea ETF (EWY) is down the most in October, declining more than 11% as of Oct. 29 as a selloff in chip stocks weighed heavily on Korean stocks.

Meanwhile, the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF (EWT), the iShares MSCI China ETF (MCHI), and the iShares MSCI Japan ETF (EWJ) are also headed lower in October amid tech weakness and rising global inflationary pressures.

Tech Pressures, Central Bank Policies Weigh On US And Asian Stocks

Amazon.com (AMZN) reported capital expenditure of $77.3 billion in its latest quarterly results, soaring past Wall Street expectations, and leading to a $7.6 billion cash burn.

Google parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL) also maintained its full-year spending expectations, while Microsoft lowered it to $170 billion from $175 billion. Tesla pulled back its annual capex forecast to about $20 billion, even though quarterly capex increased 88% to $4.7 billion.

Major chip stocks, including Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Micron Technology (MU), and Intel Corp. (INTC), are also set to end the month lower.

The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at the 3.75%-4.00% target range in its October meeting, saying it would wait for more economic cues before another change.

Top ETF Stories of October

October has been anything but smooth for Wall Street, as the tech-heavy focus on big U.S. indexes has hit the stock market. Overall, State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust SPY has gained 0.6% over the past month (as of Oct. 29, 2026), while State Street SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust DIA has advanced 1.8%, as the index has relatively less exposure to high-flying tech stocks.  

Meanwhile, the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 ETF Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 QQQ has lost about 3.3%. The key issue is that investors are increasingly questioning whether the massive spending on AI will generate enough profits to justify current valuations. 

AI's Cursed October

The tech sector and AI trade have struggled in October. The month saw AI-driven vulnerabilities that led to a series of high-impact cybersecurity incidents, a trend dubbed "Black October." The term refers to a series of high-impact cybersecurity incidents in October 2026 that were accelerated by AI. 

Meanwhile, the AI debt boom remains a key concern. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to around 5.3% at the start of the month, reviving concerns about borrowing costs and the massive debt financing used to build AI data centers.  

Investors have been constantly reassessing technology valuations amid rising rates and heavy corporate borrowing. Roundhill Generative AI & Technology ETF CHAT is off 12.6% over the past month (as of Oct. 29, 2026) 

Cybersecurity: The AI Winner of October 

AI is introducing new cybersecurity threats while creating significant long-term growth opportunities for cybersecurity companies and ETFs. Following the Hugging Face incident, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta have all reported instances of AI agents escaping test sandboxes and accessing external systems. 

Meanwhile, cybercriminals are leveraging AI to execute increasingly sophisticated attacks, making cybersecurity spending a business necessity rather than a discretionary expense. 

State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF XLK is off more than 3% over the past month (as of Oct. 29, 2026), whileWisdomTree Cybersecurity Fund (WCBR) has surged about 10.3% during the same timeframe. 

Alphabet's Plunge After Earnings: Cash Generation Is Now an Issue

Alphabet GOOGL plunged about 13% Thursday (at the time of writing) after its third-quarter results, putting it on track for its worst day since going public in 2004, as quoted on Yahoo Finance.  

The stock lost about $524 billion in market value at its low, the second-largest one-day loss for a U.S.-listed company after NVIDIA's $593 billion wipeout in January 2025 (the day China's DeepSeek's cheaper AI model claims upset AI investors).
